paragraphs.text: Many cities that removed their tram lines in the middle of the twentieth century are now building new ones. The old trams were often seen as slow and noisy, and buses, which did not need rails, appeared more flexible.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: The modern tram is a very different vehicle. It is quiet, has low floors that make it easy to board with a pushchair or wheelchair, and can carry more than three times as many passengers as a bus.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Supporters also point to its effect on property. In several French cities, the value of homes and shops near new tram stops rose faster than in other areas, and some businesses moved specifically to be close to the line.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Trams are not cheap, however. Laying the track means digging up streets and moving pipes and cables, and a single kilometre can cost many times more than a bus lane. Construction may disrupt traffic and local shops for several years.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: For this reason some cities have chosen a compromise: buses that run in their own lanes and stop at raised platforms, offering some of the comfort of a tram at a fraction of the cost. Critics argue that these lanes are easily taken over by other traffic when budgets are cut.
paragraphs.label: E

paragraphs.text: Perhaps the strongest argument for trams is psychological. Because the rails are permanent, residents and investors trust that the service will still be there in twenty years, which is not true of a bus route that can be changed overnight.
paragraphs.label: F

items.prompt: a reason why trams were removed in the past
a comparison of how many people different vehicles can carry
the risk that a cheaper alternative may not be protected in future
the idea that permanent infrastructure makes people feel confident
the problems caused while tram lines are being built

groups.instruction: Questions 1–5. The reading passage has six paragraphs, A–F. Which paragraph contains the following information? Write the correct letter, A–F.
